styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Museums, studios and the movie-star walk of fame.

styles.label: Coast
styles.blurb: Santa Monica, Venice and Malibu sunsets.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Tacos, food trucks and Koreatown nights.

stays.why: Central for Metro rail, museums and food halls; good value on weekends.
Walk to the Walk of Fame and the studios; easy subway rides downtown.
Beach and pier on the doorstep; light rail to downtown LA.
Nightlife, restaurants and walkable streets between Hollywood and the beaches.

food: Try tacos and burritos at taquerias and food trucks; a meal often costs $10–15.
Koreatown is great for late-night Korean BBQ and noodles; expect $25–40 a person.
Grand Central Market downtown has many stalls under one roof; budget $10–20.
Book popular dinner spots ahead, especially on weekends in West Hollywood.
Beach towns have casual seafood and burger shacks; check hours, some close early.
more_time: Add a day for the Getty Center or the Getty Villa; both are free or low cost, check parking fees.
Swap a beach afternoon for a studio tour in Burbank or Hollywood; book ahead.
Take a harbour boat from San Pedro to Catalina Island if you have a full extra day.

recommend.why: Three nights lets you see Hollywood and downtown, then slow down at the beach without long drives every day.

month_notes: January: cool days around 19°C, nights near 8°C. Bring a jacket; some rain.
February: similar to January, mild days and cool nights. A few wet days.
March: warming to about 21°C; more rain days than mid-year, pack a light layer.
April: pleasant, highs near 24°C and little rain. Good for walking and beaches.
May: mild and mostly dry; mornings can be overcast near the coast.
June: warm, highs around 28°C; coastal fog often clears by afternoon.
July: hot inland near 31°C; beaches cooler. Very little rain.
August: the hottest month, highs near 32°C. Plan shade and water.
September: still hot at about 31°C; evenings start to cool.
October: comfortable highs near 28°C, dry and good for sightseeing.
November: cooler, about 24°C, with a few rain days returning.
December: back to about 19°C days and 8°C nights; expect some rain.

climate_guide.summary: Warm and mostly dry, with mild winters and hot, sunny summers. Coastal areas stay cooler than inland.

items.title: Best time: April to June and September to October
items.text: Mild to warm days with little rain. Good for both sightseeing and the beach.

items.title: Hot late summer
items.text: July and August reach about 31–32°C inland. Beaches are cooler; carry water and seek shade.

items.title: Coastal fog
items.text: Mornings near Santa Monica and Venice can be grey in late spring and early summer; it often clears later.

items.title: Rain is light
items.text: Most rain falls between November and March, usually a few days a month. An umbrella is handy in winter.

items.title: Cool winter nights
items.text: January and December nights drop to about 8°C. Pack a warm layer for evenings.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light layers, sunglasses and sunscreen; a jacket for winter nights and coastal fog.

transit.best: Ride apps or a rental car for most trips; Metro rail for downtown, Hollywood and Santa Monica.

modes.text: Subway and light rail link Downtown, Hollywood, Santa Monica and Long Beach. Fares about $1.75 per ride.
Metro buses cover the whole sprawl. Use a TAP card or contactless tap on rail and bus.
Taxis are metered and costlier than apps. Uber and Lyft operate widely and are the usual choice.
Driving is fastest off-peak, but freeways jam roughly 7–10am and 3–7pm.
Pleasant in beach towns and Hollywood. Bikes and e-scooters are common near the coast.
No ferries serve the city centre. Harbour boats run from San Pedro to Catalina Island.
